rationale: The HB-100 base station supports a maximum of 8 bound peripherals and already has 8 bound (bound_count=8, max_devices=8). The base station log shows "pairing request rejected: E-201 capacity reached (8/8)", and the active fault code is E-201, which the KB confirms means capacity reached. The customer's new sensor is fine; an unused device (the offline "Test Sensor") must be removed to free a slot.

repair_steps: In the app, go to Device Settings for the offline 'Test Sensor' (motion_old) and select Remove Device.
Confirm removal to free a slot on the HB-100 base station.
Put the base station into pairing mode from the app (Add Device).
Hold the SYNC button on the new door sensor for 3 seconds until its LED blinks blue, keeping it within 1 metre of the base station.
Wait for pairing to complete (within 120 seconds), then move the sensor to its final location.
output.customer_reply: Thank you for your patience. Your base station has reached its maximum of 8 connected devices, which is why the new sensor won't pair. I see an unused 'Test Sensor' that is offline. I'll guide you to remove it in the app, then we'll pair your new door sensor. No need to return it.

results.text: The base station already holds its maximum number of bound peripherals. Frontline action: remove an unused device. Not an escalation case.

HB-100 supports up to 8 bound peripherals. HB-200 supports up to 16 bound peripherals. When the limit is reached, pairing a new device fails with error E-201 even if the device is in pairing mode. Remove an unused device in the app (Device Settings > Remove Device) to free a slot.

Put the base station into pairing mode from the app (Add Device). Then hold the SYNC button on the camera or sensor for 3 seconds until its LED blinks blue. Keep the peripheral within 1 metre of the base station during pairing. Pairing times out after 120 seconds. After pairing, the device can be moved to its final location.

complaint: I bought a new door sensor last week but it just won't pair. I followed the instructions and held the button. The app shows an error with a code, and I have tried both my phone and my partner's phone with the same result. Our system has grown over the years and, honestly, I don't remember how many devices we have. Do I need to return the sensor?
